skill.name: lark-task
skill.description: Manage Lark and Feishu tasks, task lists, assignees, followers, reminders, comments, status changes, and attachments through lark-cli. Use it for task creation, task search, task updates, tasklist organization, and workspace task reporting.
skill.summary: Create, update, search, and organize Lark tasks and task lists with lark-cli.
skill.author: larksuite

security_audit.summary: AI review found that the static alerts are documentation artifacts: Markdown links, code spans, example AppLinks, and lark-cli usage notes. No prompt injection attempt, data-exfiltration intent, executable payload, or obfuscated code was found in the reviewed files. The skill still performs Lark task read and write actions through lark-cli, so users should confirm write operations and review Lark permissions.

remediation.issue: Parent-directory references to shared Lark guidance may confuse package-level scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Declare the shared guidance as a marketplace dependency or duplicate the required authentication notes inside the skill package.

remediation.issue: The skill can perform Lark task write operations when users request them.
remediation.suggestion: Keep explicit confirmation steps for task creation, updates, assignment changes, completion changes, comments, and attachment uploads.

content.user_title: Manage Lark Tasks from Claude or Codex
content.value_statement: Teams lose time switching between chat, task lists, and project trackers. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code create, update, search, and organize Lark tasks through lark-cli.
actual_capabilities: Create Lark tasks with summaries, descriptions, due dates, assignees, followers, and tasklist links.
Update, complete, reopen, comment on, and organize existing tasks by GUID or task AppLink.
Search tasks and list tasks assigned to or related to the current user.
Create task lists and manage tasklist members, sections, and task placement.
Upload one local attachment to a task or task delivery resource using a relative path.
Document native task API resources and required Lark task permission scopes.
limitations: Requires lark-cli, an authenticated Lark account, and the correct task API permissions.
Can only access tasks, task lists, users, and attachments allowed by the active Lark identity.
Write operations should be confirmed before execution because they modify workspace task data.
Attachment upload supports one local file per call, up to 50 MB, from the current working directory.

use_cases.title: Create team tasks from chat
use_cases.description: Turn a short request into a Lark task with assignees, due dates, followers, and a tasklist.

use_cases.title: Review personal work queues
use_cases.description: List incomplete tasks assigned to the current user and summarize deadlines for planning.

use_cases.title: Maintain project task lists
use_cases.description: Create task lists, add existing tasks, manage members, and keep project work organized.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple task
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Lark task called Prepare weekly update for me, due this Friday.

prompt_templates.title: Find pending work
prompt_templates.prompt: Show my incomplete Lark tasks due this week, with task links and due times.

prompt_templates.title: Update several tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Move these Lark tasks to next Monday and add a short comment explaining the schedule change.

prompt_templates.title: Organize a launch list
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a launch task list, add tasks for review, deployment, and announcement, assign owners, and add reminders.

output_examples.input: Create a task for me to review the Q3 forecast by Friday.
output_examples.output: Created the task Review the Q3 forecast, assigned it to you, set the due date to Friday, and returned the Lark task link.

output_examples.input: Show my incomplete tasks due this week.
output: Found three incomplete tasks due this week.
Each result includes the task title, due time, owner details when available, and a direct Lark link.

output_examples.input: Add this file to the design review task.
output_examples.output: Uploaded the selected local file as one task attachment and returned the attachment name, size, identifier, and link when available.

best_practices: Confirm the exact task, tasklist, members, and due date before running any write operation.
Use task GUIDs or Lark task AppLinks instead of display task numbers.
Filter personal task lists with completion and date limits to avoid noisy results.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for meeting-minute todo items when the minutes workflow owns the todo.
Do not fetch every related task when the user gave a clear time boundary.
Do not upload absolute paths or files outside the current working directory.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages Lark and Feishu tasks, task lists, members, comments, reminders, status changes, and attachments.

faq.question: Does it require Lark authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It depends on lark-cli and the active Lark identity with the required task permissions.

faq.question: Can it modify workspace data?
faq.answer: Yes. Creating, updating, assigning, completing, reopening, commenting, and uploading attachments are write operations.

faq.question: Can it search my tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It can search tasks by keyword and filters, and it can list tasks assigned to or related to the current user.

faq.question: Can it attach files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can upload one local file per call when the file is inside the current working directory.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
